evidence.excerpt: Krisztina Kiss received her Dipl.Ing. degree in computer engineering from the University of Novi Sad in 2001 and her PhD in electrical and computer engineering from the same institution in 2008, with a dissertation on statistical traffic profiling in industrial Ethernet networks. She joined the Department of Computing and Control Engineering as an assistant professor in 2009 and was promoted to full professor in 2020. Her research group focuses on unsupervised anomaly detection and one-class classification for industrial control system protocol traffic, using statistical baseline modelling, kernel methods, and lightweight online learning algorithms suited to constrained embedded environments. She teaches courses on network security, operating systems, and industrial communication protocols. The group operates a dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure for long-term dataset collection.
